name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Rupiah holds near record lows around 18,230/$ after Bank Indonesia's rate rise; no EM default or IMF rescue found
state: The rupiah traded near 18,230 per dollar on 16 Nov, close to historic lows (Investortrust), after sliding past 18,000 on 12 Nov on bets of further US rate rises and domestic politics (Jakarta Post). It has held roughly steady since Bank Indonesia raised its rate on 18 Nov and is short of a 10% fall in a month. No major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 23 Nov, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: A weaker rupiah raises import costs in Indonesia and can make travel there cheaper for visitors. No wider emerging-market crisis is under way.
rubric_hit: No major EM currency down >10% in a month, no IMF emergency support = Normal

sources.title: Investortrust — FTSE Russell status retention cushions rupiah slide toward record lows
The Jakarta Post — Rupiah touches new low on Fed hike bets, politics

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
